autoTier: the supported-key matrix lists Copilot CLI and VS Code, and marks the GitHub Copilot app, Copilot cloud agent, and JetBrains IDEs as not supported.
policies.location: For a server-managed deployment: copilot/managed-settings.json in the designated .github-private repository.

knownLimitations: model sets the default for new conversations; users can still select a different model per conversation.

autoTier only applies when the selected model is auto; it does not select the model itself. A plain tier string locks the tier against user and repository overrides; overridable provides an overridable default.

The Auto model-selection guide says Auto tiers are available in the GitHub Copilot app, but the managed-settings supported-key matrix marks autoTier as not supported there. Managed autoTier support in the app remains unresolved; do not infer it from availability in the model picker.
Auto selects only supported models permitted by the user's plan and administrator policies; a preset does not replace model-access policies.
policies.releaseStatus: Support is key- and client-specific; no blanket release-status claim.
policies.propagation: Server-managed settings arrive within about an hour; restarting the client or signing in again triggers an immediate refresh.

prerequisites: An approved investigation purpose and authorized access before reviewing real data.

Sample events are plain-language fictional records, not GitHub event names or an API schema.
Session-level streaming is documented as preview with enterprise eligibility restrictions; it is not configured in this lab.

policies.name: Organization billing for Copilot CLI automation and code review
policies.requiredPermissions: Enterprise owner; organization owner for delegated organization settings.
supportedSurfaces: Copilot CLI in GitHub Actions using GITHUB_TOKEN in organization-owned repositories.
Copilot code review billing for requests associated with organization members with paid Copilot licenses.
policies.location: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients; Agents > Copilot code review
prerequisites: An assigned test enterprise and organizations.
AI credits paid usage is required for organization-billed code review.
knownLimitations: CLI organization billing is separate from user-authenticated CLI usage. GITHUB_TOKEN workflows in organization-owned repositories require Allow use of Copilot CLI billed to the organization.
Organization-billed CLI usage does not count against individual user-level budgets.
Choosing organization billing for licensed members' code reviews changes billing, not access. It applies to manually requested and automatic reviews.
Other bot-triggered reviews and eligible reviews for users without licenses can also bill the organization; retaining member billing does not eliminate those charges.
Organization-billed code reviews use applicable organization, cost-center, or enterprise spending controls rather than the member's ULB.
policies.releaseStatus: No blanket release-status claim made.
policies.propagation: No fixed propagation duration established from reviewed sources.

policies.name: Enterprise billing manager access
policies.requiredPermissions: Enterprise owner coordinating with the identity-provider administrator for Enterprise Managed Users.
supportedSurfaces: Enterprise People > Administrators for enterprises using personal accounts; identity-provider assignments for Enterprise Managed Users.
policies.location: Enterprise > People > Administrators
prerequisites: An assigned test enterprise with administrator access for a view-only walkthrough; do not invite anyone or change roles.
knownLimitations: Billing managers can view and manage enterprise billing settings; this is not read-only reporting access.
An invited administrator must accept the emailed invitation before gaining access.
Enterprise Managed Users billing managers can only be added or removed through the identity provider.
Role assignment does not establish an internal approval process or attest that billing changes were reviewed.

policies.name: AI credit payment methods and Azure billing
policies.requiredPermissions: GitHub account owner for an Azure connection, coordinating with an Azure subscription owner and tenant administrator as needed.
supportedSurfaces: Enterprise payment information and cost center Azure subscription routing.
policies.location: Enterprise > Billing & Licensing > Payment information; Cost centers
prerequisites: Finance approval of the account, eligible payment method, and any Azure subscription.
The lab already has an Azure subscription; no payment or subscription changes are permitted.
knownLimitations: Credit card and PayPal are supported for unmanaged accounts, or as nonrecurring methods for managed accounts. Invoice and ACH are for managed accounts only.
Azure subscription eligibility and account restrictions apply; connecting a subscription does not establish entitlement to a discount.

Separate cost centers can route usage to different Azure subscriptions. Without its own subscription, a cost center uses the enterprise subscription; invalid or deleted cost centers also fall back for future usage.
policies.releaseStatus: No preview claim made.
policies.propagation: No fixed connection or billing propagation duration established from reviewed sources.

policies.name: AI credit consumption and spending guardrails
policies.requiredPermissions: Enterprise owner or enterprise billing manager.
supportedSurfaces: Per-user Copilot AI credit consumption, bundled metered AI-credit spending across products, and documented SKU-level controls including Code Security AI Credits.
policies.location: Enterprise > Billing & Licensing > Budgets and alerts
prerequisites: An assigned test account where Bundled AI credits budget controls are available.
Choose budget amounts, scopes, and alert recipients in the test environment; zero amounts may be used to explore blocking.
knownLimitations: User-level budgets cap each user's included and metered AI credit consumption and always hard-stop. Individual ULBs take precedence over ULBs assigned to cost centers, then universal ULBs.

Under pooled billing, cost-center, organization, and enterprise budgets cap metered charges after pool exhaustion, not license fees or each user's included consumption. Stop usage when budget limit is reached must be enabled for enforcement.
A ULB assigned to a cost center is a per-user limit, not the cost center's total metered-spending budget.
Separate included usage controls cap a cost center's draw from included credits; configure them only for intentionally retained pooled billing, not the announced non-pooled model.
A reached user-level limit is not overridden by remaining group or enterprise budget.
Bundled AI-credit budgets include other AI-credit products. If bundled and SKU-level hard budgets both apply, exhausting either can block the workload.
User-level budget alerts are not consistently available; also monitor enterprise or cost-center usage.
policies.releaseStatus: No preview claim made for this exercise.
policies.propagation: No fixed propagation duration established from reviewed sources.

policies.name: Cost centers and allocation
policies.requiredPermissions: Enterprise owner or enterprise billing manager for this exercise.
supportedSurfaces: Cost attribution using users, enterprise teams, and licensing organizations.
policies.location: Enterprise > Billing and licensing > Cost centers
prerequisites: A preconfigured billing connection, approved membership, and a known licensing source.
Permission to inspect or create a dedicated cost center without moving shared resources.
knownLimitations: Cost centers attribute spending; internal showback or chargeback is a finance process, not a promise of a separate invoice.
Direct user assignments take precedence over conflicting enterprise-team assignments. Among teams assigned to different cost centers, the team created first applies.
Enterprise-team membership stays current automatically as people join or leave the team.
A resource belongs to one cost center; assigning it elsewhere moves it. Allocation changes affect future usage.
Cost centers apply to metered usage, not volume or subscription billing. Organization attribution follows the billed licensing organization.
policies.releaseStatus: No preview claim made for this exercise.
policies.propagation: Team membership stays current automatically; no fixed propagation duration is asserted.

policies.name: AI consumption and billing reports
policies.requiredPermissions: Enterprise owner or enterprise billing manager for dashboard inspection in this exercise.
supportedSurfaces: AI usage dashboard, one downloadable AI usage report in CSV format, chart data exports, broader metered billing reports, CSV billing report API, and a separate budgets API for budget state.
policies.location: Enterprise > Billing & Licensing > Usage > AI usage or Metered usage
prerequisites: An agreed reporting period and filters.
Live usage when available; an empty sandbox remains missing live data, not proof of zero production cost.
knownLimitations: Enterprise owners and billing managers can filter AI usage by user. Organization owners need a usage report for per-user consumption.
There is one AI usage report, covering up to 31 days with user, model, and token detail. Summarized and detailed metered reports are broader billing reports, not extra AI-credit report types.
Emailed report download links expire after 24 hours. Chart data exports reflect the selected chart view, not necessarily the full report.

The usage report exports API accepts ai_credit report requests, processes them asynchronously, and returns status and download_urls. Inspect processing, completed, or failed status before downloading.

The budgets API provides configured amounts, enforcement settings, and consumed amounts for assessing budget state; these are not a substitute for billing-report data. The user filter returns effective_budget details for the specified login.
Reports and budget state support recorded cost and budget-position views, not session histories or proof of a real-time synchronized balance.
Gross consumption is not the same as net billed amounts. Spending alone does not establish engineering impact.
Exports may contain user-level information. Keep real reports and credentials outside the canvas and repository.
policies.releaseStatus: No blanket release-status claim; consult the linked endpoint reference.
policies.propagation: No fixed reporting delay is asserted. Record the available period and missing data.
